page: Google Cloud Platform n2d-highmem-4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance designed for workloads requiring a higher memory-to-vCPU ratio. It features 4 vCPUs and 32 GB of RAM, providing 8 GB of memory per core. The instance is powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor built on the x86_64 architecture, utilizing 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core under a dedicated CPU allocation model. The cache hierarchy consists of 32 KB of L1d cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. This instance does not include bundled local storage or GPU accelerators.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong single-core CPU performance, with stress-ng single-core tests placing in the top 25%. Conversely, multi-core performance is relatively weak, scoring in the bottom 25% on stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core tests. Memory bandwidth read speeds are also in the bottom 25%, though large block write bandwidth and Passmark memory scores perform at an average level. The processor supports hardware-accelerated cryptography via AES, VAES, and SHA_NI instruction sets, alongside AVX, BMI2, and FMA, but lacks AVX-512 and AMX extensions.

Given the high memory density relative to the compute resources, the n2d-highmem-4 is qualitatively cost-efficient for workloads requiring substantial memory footprints without intensive parallel processing demands. It is suited for memory-bound applications, light database operations, single-threaded data processing, and basic web serving. The lack of local storage and lower multi-threaded performance make it less optimal for heavy parallel computing, large-scale compilation, or high-throughput database clusters.
